sha.about.limit: A hash proves a mod has not changed; it does not prove the mod was safe to begin with. Re-hashing accepts the files as they are now as the new reference.
sha.about.strict: With strict integrity on (Settings), a mod without a valid hash cannot be enabled until it is hashed.

tut.basics.activate.s1.text:
Activating a mod does this automatically:
  • 1. BMM reads the mod's mapping plan
  • 2. It fingerprints (SHA-256) every file it will overwrite
  • 3. Originals are saved to your Backup Folder
  • 4. Mod files are copied to the destination folder
Deactivating restores the originals.
:tip:

Your game files are always recoverable: BMM keeps 3 backup layers.
tut.basics.activate.s1.title: What happens when you flip it
tut.basics.activate.s2.action: Flip the toggle switch on any mod card to ON.
tut.basics.activate.s2.text: Use the toggle switch on the left of any mod card in the Library. BMM copies the mod's files and shows a progress bar for large mods. The card turns green and shows an activation order number (#1, #2…) when done.
tut.basics.activate.s2.title: Turn one on
tut.basics.activate.s3.action: Flip the same mod's toggle switch back to OFF.
tut.basics.activate.s3.text: Toggle the switch back Off. BMM looks up the backup it saved during activation and restores every original file. The order number disappears and the card returns to inactive state.
tut.basics.activate.s3.title: Turn it back off
tut.basics.activate.s4.text: When two active mods touch the same game file, the one with the higher activation order number wins (activated later = higher priority). You can see each mod's order number on its card, and reorder by dragging from the detail panel.
tut.basics.activate.s4.title: Order decides who wins
tut.basics.activate.title: Turning mods on
tut.basics.conflicts.s1.text: A conflict is when two active mods write the same game file. BMM shows a badge on the mod card: Intra = a clash inside the same mod; Inter = a file touched by two different mods. Your demo mods both ship Mods/shared/config.ini, hence the Inter badge highlighted here.
tut.basics.conflicts.s1.title: Spotting a conflict
tut.basics.conflicts.s2.text: In Settings → Storage, the I/O Limiter caps disk throughput during activation to prevent system lag on slow drives or NAS setups. Run the built-in Benchmark first to find the best limit for your hardware.
tut.basics.conflicts.s2.title: Keeping the disk usable
tut.basics.conflicts.title: Conflicts and disk load
tut.basics.integrity.s1.text:
Every file BMM tracks gets a SHA-256 hash, a fingerprint of its exact bytes. Change one byte and the hash changes.

BMM records it when a mod is added, then recomputes it to know for sure if a file is still the one you installed.
:tip:

Hashes catch silent corruption: bad downloads, game patches, disk errors.
tut.basics.integrity.s1.title: A fingerprint per file

tut.basics.integrity.s2.text:
If a mod misbehaves after a game update, click Verify in the Library toolbar. Each file is flagged:
  • OK: matches the stored hash :ok:
  • Modified: changed since install
  • Missing: deleted or moved

tut.basics.map.s1.text: Mods are not always packaged the way the game expects (files in MyMod/data/…, at the root, nested deep…). The Mapper points each mod file or folder to its place in the game, without renaming or moving the originals. BMM records “this mod folder → goes there in the game” and applies it on activation.
tut.basics.map.s1.title: When a mod is packed wrong
tut.basics.map.s2.text: Choose a profile from this dropdown. It tells the Mapper which game folder to load, so the right-hand panel fills with that game’s real directory structure. Everything you map is saved per-profile.
tut.basics.map.s2.title: Step 1: pick a profile
tut.basics.map.s3.text: The Mapper is split in two. Left = the mod (the files exactly as the mod ships them). Right = the game (the real folders on disk where files must land). Mapping is simply drawing a line from a spot on the left to a folder on the right.
tut.basics.map.s3.title: The two panels
tut.basics.map.s4.text: Choose a mod in the left dropdown to see its file tree. An orange dot marks the mod’s root, a green dot a subfolder. Are the files where the game expects them, or one level too deep?
tut.basics.map.s4.title: Step 2: pick a mod
tut.basics.map.s5.text: Click a file or folder on the LEFT (hold Ctrl for several), then double-click the destination folder on the RIGHT. BMM links them. Untouched files keep their original path.
tut.basics.map.s5.title: Step 3: select left, double-click right
tut.basics.map.s6.text: Click Preview (Aperçu Final) to see every mod file at its final game path: green = correct, orange/red = misplaced or conflicting. Nothing is written yet.
tut.basics.map.s5b.title: Need a folder that isn’t there?
tut.basics.map.s5b.text: Need a folder the archive didn't include? Click New folder (highlighted). Like every mapper change it's staged until you Save.
tut.basics.map.s5b.action: Click New folder and name it to stage a folder.
tut.basics.map.s6.title: Step 4: check the preview
tut.basics.map.s7.action: Click the Preview button to open the full mapping diagnostic.
tut.basics.map.s7.text: Happy with the preview? Click Apply Structure (Appliquer Structure) at the top to save the mapping. Activating the mod then places its files where you mapped them.
tut.basics.map.s7.title: Step 5: apply
tut.basics.map.title: Mapping a mod’s structure
tut.basics.meta.desc: Learn what BMM can do: isolated profiles per game, automatic mod scanning, safe activation with full backup, file integrity verification, conflict detection, and shared folders for multi-profile setups.
tut.basics.meta.title: The basics of modding with BMM
tut.basics.modpacks.s1.text: A Modpack is a curated group of mods that can be toggled on or off together with a single click. Perfect for managing 'load orders' or themed sets of mods for different scenarios.
tut.basics.modpacks.s1.title: A named group of mods
tut.basics.modpacks.s2.action: Go to Modpacks, click "Create Modpack", add a few mods with "Add Mods", then click "Save Modpack".
tut.basics.modpacks.s2.text:
Open Modpacks and click Create Modpack. In the editor:
  • Give the pack a name (description optional).
  • Click Add Mods to pick mods; each has a Remove button.
  • Click Save Modpack, or Cancel.
Enabling a modpack turns all its mods on; disabling turns them off.
tut.basics.modpacks.s2.title: Create one
tut.basics.modpacks.title: Making a modpack
tut.basics.profiles.s1.text: A Profile is a workspace for a specific game configuration. Each one has its own game path, mods folder, and backup directory. Think of it as a dedicated slot for each game you mod.
tut.basics.profiles.s1.title: Why a profile comes first
tut.basics.profiles.s2.action: Open Profiles, click "Create a profile", fill the four fields explained above, then click Create.
tut.basics.profiles.s2.text: Open Profiles and click Create a profile. Fill in the fields below, then click Create.
tut.basics.profiles.s2.title: Create your first profile
tut.basics.profiles.s3.text:
Three folders matter for every profile:
  • Destination folder: where mods deploy, usually the game's root (with the .exe)
  • Mods Folder: where your mods live; BMM scans it
  • Backup Folder: where BMM saves original game files
:warn:

Never share a Mods Folder between two profiles.
tut.basics.profiles.s3.title: The three folders it needs
tut.basics.profiles.s4.text: Each profile can have a custom background and a color accent. Click the Edit icon (pencil) on any profile card to personalize it. BMM includes a built-in cropping tool for background images.
tut.basics.profiles.s4.title: Give it a colour you won’t confuse
tut.basics.profiles.title: Profiles
tut.basics.scan.s0.text: Go to Profiles and make sure at least one profile is active (highlighted with a colored border). The active profile defines where BMM looks for mods and where it installs them. Without an active profile, Library and Mapper won't work.
tut.basics.scan.s0.title: Check which profile is active
tut.basics.scan.s1.text: A scan registers every subfolder of your Mods Folder as a mod. No file is moved, copied or modified.
tut.basics.scan.s1.title: Why BMM scans first
tut.basics.scan.s2.action: Click the Scan button in the Library toolbar.
tut.basics.scan.s2.text: Switch to the Library tab and click Scan in the toolbar. BMM walks your Mods Folder, discovers every subfolder, and populates the list. Each entry shows name, size, file count, and activation status.
tut.basics.scan.s2.title: Run your first scan
tut.basics.scan.s3.text: Click + Add mod in the toolbar to pick a folder or a .zip archive. BMM copies it into your Mods Folder and registers it, no scan needed.
tut.basics.scan.s3.title: Add a mod by hand
tut.basics.scan.title: Finding your mods
tut.basics.shared.s1.text: Sharing a single Mods Folder between two profiles is strongly discouraged. You risk activating a mod intended for another game, which can corrupt your installation. BMM will warn you if you try to share a folder.
tut.basics.shared.s1.title: :warn: Two profiles, one game folder
tut.basics.shared.s2.text: If two game versions use identical file structures (e.g. an expansion and its base game), sharing is possible. Keep the game paths different and always verify the active profile before enabling mods.
tut.basics.shared.s2.title: When it is safe anyway
tut.basics.shared.title: Sharing one folder (optional)
tut.other.benchmark.s1.text: Mod activation involves copying potentially large files. Knowing your disk's real-world speed lets BMM set sensible I/O limits so activation does not degrade your system performance.
tut.other.benchmark.s1.title: Measure instead of guessing
tut.other.benchmark.s2.text: In Settings & Other, open the Performance & Benchmark section and click Open Benchmark. It shows live CPU, RAM and Disk I/O to help tune the I/O Limiter.
tut.other.benchmark.s2.title: Run one
tut.other.benchmark.title: Benchmark
tut.other.storage.title: Storage and Smart I/O
tut.other.storage.s1.title: Why mods can slow your PC
tut.other.storage.s1.text: Activating mods copies many files, which can make a slow drive stutter. Smart I/O paces those copies so mods apply in the background without freezing your PC.
tut.other.storage.s2.title: Calibrate once
tut.other.storage.s2.text: Open Storage in Settings and start Auto-Calibration. It tests each drive and suggests a read/write limit. Run it once.
tut.other.storage.s3.title: Limits are per disk
tut.other.storage.s3.text: Each drive gets its own ceiling, so a fast NVMe isn't held back by a slow external disk. A limit of 0 means unlimited. If activation ever feels heavy, lower the limit on that disk; if your hardware is quick and you want maximum speed, raise it or set 0.
tut.other.backup.title: Data and backup
tut.other.backup.s1.title: Your safety net
tut.other.backup.s1.text: BMM can save your profiles, mods, modpacks, plugins and settings to a single file. Do it before any big change: it's the cheapest insurance in the app.
tut.other.backup.s2.title: Export everything
tut.other.backup.s2.text: Open Data in Settings and click Export. Keep the file somewhere safe.
tut.other.backup.s3.title: Import to restore
tut.other.backup.s3.text: To roll back, click Import and pick an exported file. It also moves your setup to another PC.
tut.other.bugreport.f.attach: Screenshots, logs and the crash zip. Drag them in or click to browse. The bar shows the size budget left.
tut.other.bugreport.f.desc: What you expected and what happened instead. The gauge below rewards this one the most, because it is the part nobody can reconstruct for you.
tut.other.bugreport.f.quality: How complete the report is, live. It is a hint, never a gate: you can always send. Click the tip and it takes you to the field it is asking for.
tut.other.bugreport.f.send: Sends it. If BetterCommunity is offline, it goes out on the next start.
tut.other.bugreport.f.steps: Reproduction steps, one per line. The single most useful thing in a bug report: a problem someone can reproduce is a problem someone can fix.
tut.other.bugreport.f.title: One line naming the problem. It is what the team reads first, so “profile switch loses my load order” beats “bug”.
tut.other.bugreport.s1.text: Report to BetterCommunity from inside the app, no browser or account needed. Pick a kind: Suggestion (an idea), Bug (something wrong) or Crash (BMM closed by itself). After a crash, BMM offers to attach the report on the next launch.
tut.other.bugreport.s1.title: Found something broken?
tut.other.bugreport.s2.text: Settings & Other → Feedback. “Report a bug” opens the form; “Send feedback” opens the same form on the Suggestion kind. Nothing is sent until you press Send, and you can read everything that will travel before you do.
tut.other.bugreport.s2.title: Send it without leaving BMM
tut.other.bugreport.s3.text: Under Attachments you can add diagnostics (BMM version, OS, recent log lines). It is opt-in and shown before sending. Logs can hold file paths, screenshots whatever was on screen.
tut.other.bugreport.s3.title: Diagnostics, and what actually leaves your machine
tut.other.bugreport.s4.text: A report written offline is kept and sent at the next start, so a bad connection is never a reason not to write. If sending keeps failing and you want to know why, “Test the endpoint” in the Feedback panel says whether BetterCommunity is reachable, unreachable, or simply not configured for this build.
tut.other.bugreport.s4.title: Nothing gets lost
tut.other.bugreport.title: Reporting a bug
tut.other.launchpack.s1.text: A BMM Launch Pack is a one-click shortcut that starts multiple applications or games at the same time. Great for launching your game alongside companion tools (overlay, capture software, voice chat) with a single icon.
tut.other.launchpack.s1.title: One click, everything opens
tut.other.launchpack.s2.text: Go to Settings & Other in the sidebar. Find the BMM Launch Pack section and click New Launch Pack. In the Create a Launch Pack dialog, name your pack, add the executables to launch, optionally set a custom icon, then confirm.
tut.other.launchpack.s2.title: Build one
tut.other.launchpack.title: Launch packs
tut.other.meta.desc: Comfort features: BMM Launchpack to deploy several games at once, an integrated benchmark dashboard to measure the performance impact when activating mods, and a one-click bug report system with self-attached logs.
tut.other.meta.title: The rest of BMM
tut.other.pluginsapi.title: Plugins and the API
tut.other.pluginsapi.s1.title: Extending BMM without forking it
tut.other.pluginsapi.s1.text: Community plugins extend BMM with actions, panels, integrations and more. Open the Plugins & API tab in the sidebar.
tut.other.pluginsapi.s2.title: Install a plugin
tut.other.pluginsapi.s2.text: Install plugins from the Catalog tab (card → Install) or import a .bmmplug file with the Import button. They then appear in the Installed tab. Optional: skip if the catalog is empty.
tut.other.pluginsapi.s2.action: Install or import a plugin to continue, or skip this step.
tut.other.pluginsapi.s3.title: What it is allowed to do
tut.other.pluginsapi.s3.text: Each plugin declares what it can access (files, network, shell…). The Permissions tab lets you revoke any of them. Global Trust allows all plugins at once: use with care.
tut.other.pluginsapi.s4.title: Generate a script
tut.other.pluginsapi.s4.text: The Script Generator lets you build automation scripts for your mod workflow without writing code. Pick an endpoint, add action blocks (copy, delete, run, move…), choose your output format (PowerShell, Python, Bash, Go…), and click Generate.
tut.other.pluginsapi.s5.title: The local API
tut.other.pluginsapi.s5.text: BMM runs a local HTTP API on port 51274 (configurable in Settings). The API tab lists every endpoint and lets you send test requests.
tut.other.pluginsapi.s6.title: The token, and why it exists
tut.other.pluginsapi.s6.text: All write endpoints require an API token. Go to the API tab → Settings, generate a token, and copy it. Tools that connect to BMM must include this token in the Authorization header. You can regenerate or revoke the token at any time.
tut.other.pluginsapi.s6.action: Copy your API token to continue.
tut.other.appcatalog.title: App Catalog
tut.other.appcatalog.s1.title: Tools, not mods
tut.other.appcatalog.s1.text: The App Catalog (sidebar, highlighted) lets you find, install, launch and update companion apps & tools in one click.
tut.other.appcatalog.s2.title: Find an app
tut.other.appcatalog.s2.text: Use the search box and the category / price filters to narrow the list. Tabs above switch between Browse, Installed, Favorites and History.
tut.other.appcatalog.s3.title: Install, launch, update
tut.other.appcatalog.s3.text: Each card has an action: Install downloads (and verifies, when a checksum is provided) the app and tracks its version; installed cards switch to Launch, and offer an Update when a newer version ships. Only install from sources you trust.
tut.other.appcatalog.s4.title: Where the list comes from
tut.other.appcatalog.s4.text: The Sources tab lists catalog URLs (official, partner, community). Add one for more apps, remove any that fail.
tut.other.translate.title: Translating BMM
tut.other.translate.s1.title: Translate it yourself
tut.other.translate.s1.text: BMM ships a built-in Translation Sandbox so anyone can create or fix a language without touching code. It lives in Settings.
tut.other.translate.s2.title: Open the sandbox
tut.other.translate.s2.text: Click Translation Sandbox (highlighted). Edits stay in the sandbox until you export. Pointer mode jumps to an element's key.
tut.other.translate.s3.title: Export and share
tut.other.translate.s3.text: Export your language file and share it. Others import it via bmm://language/import or the language menu.
tut.other.translate.s4.title: Thank you :heart:
tut.other.translate.s4.text: Community translations keep BMM accessible to everyone. Even fixing a few awkward strings helps a lot.
tut.other.themes.title: Themes
tut.other.themes.s1.title: Make BMM yours
tut.other.themes.s1.text: The Theme System restyles all of BMM (colours, fonts, shapes, images, icons) with no CSS knowledge. Raw CSS is still there.
tut.other.themes.s2.title: Open the theme editor
tut.other.themes.s2.text: Click Open Theme Editor (highlighted). Start from one of the built-in presets, or pick a single colour and let the auto-palette generate a full coherent dark or light theme.
tut.other.themes.s3.title: Edit any element
tut.other.themes.s3.text: Use the eyedropper, then right-click any element to change its colours, hover, CSS, icon or image. Your changes lists every edit; Discard reverts all.
tut.other.themes.s4.title: Save, share, install
tut.other.themes.s4.text: Save your theme, export it as a .bmmtheme file or copy a one-click share link, and browse the Theme Catalog for community themes.

docs.diagram.modact.node.DONE_ON.desc: The mod is live. Game files reflect this mod's content.
docs.diagram.modact.node.DISABLE.desc: User triggers mod deactivation. BMM processes each mod file one by one.
docs.diagram.modact.node.FIND_SURVIVOR.d: BMM searches other currently active mods in reverse activation order to find one that also modifies this file.
docs.diagram.modact.node.HAS_SURVIVOR: Another active mod owns this file?
docs.diagram.modact.node.HAS_SURVIVOR.de: If another active mod also modifies this file, its version takes over instead of restoring vanilla.
docs.diagram.modact.node.HAS_ORIGINAL.de: Checks if the vanilla game file was backed up when the first mod was activated.
docs.diagram.modact.node.RESTORE_MOD.des: The file from the surviving active mod is copied into the game directory.
docs.diagram.modact.node.RESTORE_ORIG.de: The original game file is restored from the _original/ backup folder.
docs.diagram.modact.node.DELETE.desc: The file was added by this mod (no vanilla version ever existed), so it is simply deleted.
docs.diagram.modact.node.DONE_OFF.desc: The mod is inactive. All its files have been restored to their previous state.
docs.modact.title: Mod Activation System
docs.modact.enable.title: Activation
docs.modact.enable.desc: When you enable a mod, BMM copies each of its files into the game directory. If a file doesn't have a vanilla backup yet, it saves one first — this guarantees you can always restore your game.
docs.modact.disable.title: Deactivation
docs.modact.disable.desc: When you disable a mod, BMM checks each file: if another active mod uses the same file, it restores that mod's version. If not, it restores the original vanilla file. If the file was added from scratch by this mod (no vanilla version), it gets deleted.
docs.modact.conflict.title: File Conflicts
docs.modact.conflict.desc: If Mod A and Mod B both modify the same file, the one activated last wins. Disabling it restores the other mod's version automatically — no manual intervention needed.
docs.modact.backup.title: Automatic Backup
docs.modact.backup.desc: The vanilla backup is created exactly once per file — the first time any mod touches it. Subsequent mods share this protection. Disabling all mods fully restores your game.
docs.modact.simple.title: Summary
docs.modact.simple.enable: Enable = backup vanilla (once) → copy mod files
docs.modact.simple.disable: Disable = restore previous version (other mod / vanilla) or delete new files
docs.diagram.lightweight.node.BACKUP.des: Original game files are protected before any modification and restored upon deactivation.
docs.diagram.lightweight.node.IO_LIMIT.d: Regulates copies to prevent system slowdown (Lag-free).
docs.diagram.lightweight.node.PROFILE.de: Each profile has its own independent storage, avoiding conflicts between different games.
docs.diagram.lightweight.node.RESTORE.de: Disabling a mod returns the game to its 100% pure original state.
docs.diagram.lightweight.node.SMART_COPY: BMM actually moves files instead of using complex or fragile virtual links.
docs.diagram.lightweight.title: Lightweight Philosophy
docs.diagram.mod_arch.node.PRIO.desc: If two mods share a file, the one enabled last (highest index) wins. This ensures that your most recent choices take precedence over base mods.
docs.diagram.mod_arch.node.SCAN.desc: Analyzes the mod folder to build a list of all files and their relative paths. It focuses purely on game assets to ensure maximum compatibility.
docs.diagram.mod_arch.node.SYNC.desc: Physically copies files to the game and saves originals in the Backup folder. This 'Root Injection' strategy ensures that the game sees the files exactly where it expects them.

docs.diagram.modpack.node.EXPORT.desc: Send your .bmp file to friends or upload it to a repository.
docs.diagram.modpack.node.HASH.desc: BMM calculates a unique signature for each mod file. This ensures everyone gets the exact same version.
docs.diagram.modpack.node.IMPORT.desc: Your friends import the .bmp. BMM reads the required hashes.
docs.diagram.modpack.node.MATCH.desc: BMM searches your local library for mods matching the pack's hashes.
docs.diagram.modpack.node.SAVE.desc: Data is compressed into a portable JSON file (.bmp).
docs.diagram.modpack.node.SELECT.desc: Choose the mods and profiles you want to include in your pack.
docs.diagram.mtime.node.COMPARE.desc: Compares OS mtime with the timestamp recorded during the last full scan.
docs.diagram.mtime.node.MOD.desc: BMM identifies the target mod files to check for potential conflicts.
docs.diagram.mtime.node.MT_CHECK.desc: Asks the OS for the 'Last Modified' timestamp (mtime) of the file.
docs.diagram.mtime.node.REHASH.desc: If the file was modified, a new BLAKE3 fingerprint is calculated and cached.
docs.diagram.mtime.node.SKIP.desc: If timestamps match, BMM skips the heavy BLAKE3 calculation. +80% speed boost.

docs.diagram.offlineMode.title: Offline Mode Detection
navigator.onLine plus the online/offline window events — only says a network interface exists, not that the internet is reachable.
docs.diagram.offlineMode.node.PROBE.desc: BMM pings two lightweight endpoints (gstatic 204 + Cloudflare trace) with a 5-second timeout. Any answer — even opaque — means online.
docs.diagram.offlineMode.node.ONLINE.des: Normal operation. A background re-check every 2 minutes catches silent drops.
docs.diagram.offlineMode.node.OFFLINE.de: Both probes failed (or the OS says no network). BMM never removes features — it pauses the online ones.
docs.diagram.offlineMode.node.BANNER.des: A discreet 'no connection' banner appears; it slides away as soon as connectivity returns.
docs.diagram.offlineMode.node.EVENT.desc: A bmm-connectivity CustomEvent tells every module about the change without any imports.
docs.diagram.offlineMode.node.GATES.desc: requireOnline() shows a warning toast and blocks the action; safeFetch() no-ops instead of throwing.
docs.diagram.offlineMode.node.PAUSED.des: Repo syncs, catalogs, update checks and other network features wait; everything local keeps working.
docs.diagram.offlineMode.node.FAST.desc: While offline, BMM re-probes every 15 seconds so recovery is quick.
docs.diagram.offlineMode.node.SLOW.desc: While online, a 2-minute re-check catches connections that died silently.
docs.diagram.telemetryPipeline.title: Telemetry Pipeline (opt-in)
docs.diagram.telemetryPipeline.node.CONS: Telemetry is strictly opt-in. Until you explicitly accept, the tracker is a no-op — nothing is buffered, nothing is sent.
docs.diagram.telemetryPipeline.node.NOTH: Declining (or never answering) collects zero data; declining also wipes anything previously buffered.
docs.diagram.telemetryPipeline.node.EVEN: Page visits, clicks (labels only — never field values), performance samples, errors. No file paths, no mod contents.
docs.diagram.telemetryPipeline.node.REPL: Optional rrweb replay, masked by default: mod names, profile names and paths render as ••••. Unmasking is a separate opt-in.
docs.diagram.telemetryPipeline.node.QUEU: Events buffer to a local .jsonl file capped at 10 MB. Flushed every 90 s while the window is visible.
docs.diagram.telemetryPipeline.node.ENDP: If no telemetry endpoint is configured, data never leaves the machine.
docs.diagram.telemetryPipeline.node.LOCA: The buffer just sits on disk — exportable and deletable from Settings → Privacy.
docs.diagram.telemetryPipeline.node.GZIP: One compressed batch per flush, tagged with a packet id you can later request deletion for.
docs.diagram.telemetryPipeline.node.ALLO: Only https:// endpoints (or localhost for dev) are accepted — telemetry is never sent in clear text to a remote host.
docs.diagram.telemetryPipeline.node.SERV: Receives the batch. Every packet remains individually deletable afterwards.
docs.diagram.telemetryPipeline.node.GDPR: Settings → Privacy: export the raw buffer, or request deletion of any sent packet (honoured within 72 h).
docs.diagram.i18nSystem.title: Translation (i18n) System
docs.diagram.i18nSystem.node.LANGFILES.d: One JSON per language under Lang/ — flat key→string maps plus _info (name, flag) and _synonyms metadata.
docs.diagram.i18nSystem.node.LOAD.desc: get_language_content reads each file from disk; all available languages load in parallel at startup.
docs.diagram.i18nSystem.node.DICTS.desc: In-memory maps per language. Adding a new language file makes it appear without a rebuild.
docs.diagram.i18nSystem.node.T.desc: The translation function — resolves a key and substitutes {placeholders} in a single fast pass.
docs.diagram.i18nSystem.node.CUR.desc: First try the active language's dictionary.
docs.diagram.i18nSystem.node.OUT.desc: The resolved text, ready for the DOM.
docs.diagram.i18nSystem.node.FRFALL.desc: French is the base language: any key missing from the active language falls back to the FR dictionary.
docs.diagram.i18nSystem.node.RAWKEY.desc: Last resort — the key itself is shown, which makes a missing translation easy to spot and report.
docs.diagram.i18nSystem.node.DOM.desc: applyTranslations() walks data-i18n, data-i18n-title, -placeholder, -content and -tooltip attributes.
docs.diagram.i18nSystem.node.SWITCH.desc: setLang() re-applies every translation immediately — no restart — and persists the choice.
docs.diagram.i18nSystem.node.EVENTCH.des: Dynamic modules listen for this event to re-render their own strings.
docs.diagram.i18nSystem.node.SYN.desc: _synonyms groups from every language merge into one map (e.g. update ↔ upgrade ↔ new version).
docs.diagram.i18nSystem.node.SEARCH.desc: The palette's and docs' semantic mode expands queries through these synonyms.

docs.diagram.perf.node.NET_IO.desc: Tracks download/upload bandwidth for syncs and mod downloads.
docs.diagram.perf.node.QUEUE.desc: Schedules copy jobs so they don't all hit the disk at once.
docs.diagram.perf.node.STATS.desc: Turns the raw numbers into the graphs shown in the UI.
docs.diagram.perf.node.THROTTLE.desc: Adds tiny pauses (backpressure) to stay under your speed cap.

docs.diagram.premium.node.DETECT.desc: Continuously checks if the cursor returns to the target area during the wait.

docs.diagram.custom.node.DESC.desc: Text metadata (profile name, notes) written directly to the database.
docs.diagram.custom.node.B64.desc: Image is read and encoded as a Base64 string for in-memory processing.
docs.diagram.custom.node.CROP.desc: Image is cropped and resized to the required dimensions (square icon or banner).

docs.diagram.sync.node.CHECK_LOCAL.desc: Scans what's already on disk and computes each file's fingerprint, so BMM knows exactly what it has.
docs.diagram.sync.node.CLEAN.desc: Removes local files the remote no longer lists, freeing the space they took.
docs.diagram.sync.node.CLEANUP.desc: Deletes the temporary working files and finalizes the sync.

docs.diagram.sync.node.SCAN.desc: Walks the mod folders to index every file already present.

docs.basic.backup.a2: Upon deactivating the mod, the original file is restored, leaving your game intact with no data loss.
docs.basic.conflict.a1: BMM uses a stacking system. If two mods touch the same file, the last one defined takes priority.
docs.basic.conflict.a2: The application remembers everything it replaces in its local logs.
docs.basic.conflict.a3: By deactivating the « priority » mod, the previously activated mod's file is automatically restored!

docs.basic.integrity.a2: The system identifies files that have been modified, deleted, or added without authorization.

docs.basic.links.a4: Links to specialized forums (Nexus, DCS). No native automation possible.

docs.basic.mm.a3: Allows your friends to quickly identify your configurations and import everything very easily!
docs.basic.modding.a1: Modding means modifying or adding files to the original game.
docs.basic.modding.a2: BMM simplifies the process by keeping your mods completely separate from the game in a dedicated installation folder.

docs.enableDisableDesc:
Unlike classic mod managers that create risky or unstable virtual links (symlinks), Better Mod Manager performs a smart physical copy of your files.

1. Activation: When you enable a mod, BMM analyzes the files. If they replace original game files, it discreetly copies them to your Backup folder. Then, it injects the mod files into the game.

2. Deactivation: When you disable the mod, BMM removes the mod files from the game, then instantly restores the original files from the Backup folder. Your game returns to its pure state.

Warning: Always make sure to disable a mod from the application before physically deleting its folder, otherwise the game will keep its modification files and the backup will not be restored.

docs.diagram.blake3.title: BLAKE3 Content Hashing — how BMM hashes mods
docs.diagram.blake3.node.FILES.desc: Every file in a folder mod (or a zipped mod's extracted view). Real mods are often dominated by one very large file — exactly the case BLAKE3 wins on.
docs.diagram.blake3.node.CHUNK.desc: BLAKE3 splits each file into small chunks that can be hashed independently — the basis of its parallelism.
docs.diagram.blake3.node.PAR: Hash chunks on all CPU cores
docs.diagram.blake3.node.PAR.desc: Chunks are hashed in parallel across every core (memory-mapped + rayon). A single huge file is spread over all cores — where SHA-256 stays stuck on one core.
docs.diagram.blake3.node.TREE.desc: Chunk hashes are combined pairwise up a binary tree until a single root remains — deterministic regardless of how the work was split.
docs.diagram.blake3.node.ROOT.desc: The 256-bit root hash, stored tagged as `b3:…` so its algorithm is self-describing (older untagged digests are read as SHA-256).
docs.diagram.blake3.node.INTEG.desc: Detects a tampered or corrupt mod by comparing the current digest against the stored baseline.
docs.diagram.blake3.node.CHANGE.desc: Tells BMM which files changed since the last scan (re-hashed only when the timestamp moved).
docs.diagram.blake3.node.PACK.desc: Identifies a mod's files across machines so a shared modpack resolves to the same versions everywhere.
docs.diagram.blake3.node.REPO.desc: The shared wire format keeps SHA-256: repositories publish SHA-256 hashes and delta-sync/download verification compare against them, so BMM computes SHA-256 there independently.

docs.ioLimiterDesc:
The I/O Limiter prevents BMM from overwhelming your disks during mod operations.

Why? When you enable or disable large mods (several GBs), massive file copying can slow down your entire system — games, browser, streams.

How does it work? BMM splits each copy operation into small chunks and inserts micro-pauses between them to never exceed the speed limit you've set (in MB/s). Set 0 for unlimited speed.

Built-in Benchmark — Use the 'Benchmark Speed' button in the Storage Manager to automatically measure your disk speeds. BMM will then suggest an optimal value (70% of actual speed).

Cloud / NAS Storage — BMM automatically detects cloud drives (Google Drive, OneDrive, Dropbox) and network storage (NAS). It is strongly recommended to limit speed on these drives as they are generally slower.

docs.bench.intro: The Benchmark button (activity icon) opens a two-tab panel: Live Monitor (real-time CPU / RAM / disk while you use BMM) and Benchmark (measures how fast BMM's real operations run on a controlled dataset).
docs.bench.modesB: Sandbox (default, safe): BMM generates fake mods in a temp folder — nothing of yours is touched. My mods: a profile picker appears — choose one profile, several, all, or a custom folder; BMM uses a copy of those real files as test data. docs.bench.sizeB: The size is the total volume of mod files used for the test — it's what determines how much data is actually read, copied and hashed. Larger sizes better reflect a big library (and take longer):
docs.bench.sizeCustomDoc: Custom — enter an exact target in MB (1–4096); BMM generates enough fake files (~256 KB each) to reach that total.

docs.bench.opsB: BMM's real operations, each sampled several times (median + min/max range):
docs.bench.resB: Each operation shows its median and min–max range, its throughput (MB/s) where relevant, and an explanation. Two SVG charts at the top summarise time and throughput. Copy JSON copies the full result; Export report saves a self-contained HTML report (charts + table).
docs.bench.safe: Read-only: the benchmark never modifies your mods or your game. Every operation runs in a temporary workspace.

docs.bench.faqQ1: Can the benchmark damage my mods or save?
docs.bench.faqA1: No. Even in "My mods" mode, BMM works on a copy in a temporary workspace that is deleted afterward. Your game folder and original mods are never modified.
docs.bench.faqQ2: What does the dataset size (S / M / L / XL) mean?
docs.bench.faqA2: It's the total volume of fake mod files generated for the test (≈ S 6 MB, M 48 MB, L 160 MB, XL 400 MB). Larger sizes better reflect a big library — and take longer.
docs.bench.faqQ4: BLAKE3 or SHA-256 — which does BMM use?
docs.bench.faqA4: Both, for different jobs. For local hashing (integrity, change-detection, modpack fingerprints) BMM uses BLAKE3: it's a tree hash, so one very large file is hashed across all CPU cores at once — where SHA-256 stays sequential on a single file. For the shared/wire format (repo sync, download verification) BMM keeps SHA-256. Old SHA-256 fingerprints still verify (hashes are tagged) and migrate to BLAKE3 on the next recompute.
docs.bench.faqQ3: Why do my results vary from one run to the next?
docs.bench.faqA3: Speed depends on your disk (SSD/HDD), the OS cache and current load. Each operation is sampled several times and BMM shows the median + min–max range to smooth out the variation.

faq.a1: Yes! Each profile keeps its own mod state. When you return to a profile, your enabled mods are still there, even after a restart.

faq.a3: You must first disable the mod so its files are removed from the game, then you can safely delete it.
faq.a4: Disable the mod, replace its files in the mods folder, then re-enable it. The backup will be recreated automatically.
faq.a5: BMM uses a stacked system. The last mod you enable has priority. But don't worry: if you disable it, BMM will automatically restore the previous mod's file or the original!
faq.a6: Yes! Use the Archive Explorer in the mod details to navigate folders and even open files directly.
faq.a7: It's often because the mod is very large (many files or several GBs). If the mods folder and the game are not on the same hard drive, copying may be slowed down by your drive speeds.
faq.a8: BMM checks the space before each copy. If the disk is full, activation is blocked for safety, even if alerts are disabled in the settings.
faq.a9: No. Unlike visual alerts, blocking in case of a saturated disk is vital to prevent data or system corruption.
faq.aBenchValues: The performance graph monitors the entire disk, not just BMM. If you limit BMM to 10 MB/s, but Windows, your browser, or your antivirus use 2 MB/s in the background, the graph will show 12 MB/s. BMM always strictly respects its own internal limit.
faq.aCrash: BMM uses a 'clean shutdown flag'. On each startup, it checks if the previous session ended normally. If not, a report is automatically generated.
faq.aCreatorId: The Creator ID is a hardware fingerprint BMM generates from your machine. It identifies your client to the server without a login, so the admin can whitelist or ban users even if their IP changes.
faq.aDiscord: Go to settings and toggle 'Enable Discord RPC'. If Discord is running, BMM will automatically update your status. Ensure that 'Activity Status' is public in your Discord user settings.
faq.aHidden: Not really 'hidden', but less known: auto-calibration adjusts your speed limits based on real disk load at startup.
faq.aHostOwn: Yes! BMM is designed for self-hosting. You can use any Linux VPS (Ubuntu recommended). Refer to the dedicated deployment guide in the 'Advanced' tab.
faq.aIntegrity: BMM calculates a unique cryptographic hash for every file. This ensures that mods haven't been corrupted or tampered with. The system can detect even single-bit changes, guaranteeing that what you download is exactly what the mod author intended.
faq.aIo: It prevents BMM from copying files too fast, which could lag your PC. Go to Settings → Storage Manager to adjust the speed limit per disk.
faq.aJsTs: BMM v0.9+ has migrated to TypeScript (TS) for better stability. However, the Modern ESM system requires that imports use the .js extension because they reference the final files that stay in the browser/Tauri after compilation.
faq.aLimit: BMM now includes safety features. If your free space drops below the warning threshold, you'll get a warning. If it drops below the critical threshold, installation will be blocked to protect your system.
faq.aLuxStd: The Lux version includes a web-based monitoring dashboard for your repository, ideal for visualizing server status. The STD version is ultra-lightweight, with no UI, perfect for VPS with very low RAM.
faq.aModpacks: BMM Modpacks use BLAKE3 fingerprints to uniquely identify mod files. This ensures every player uses exactly the same version, regardless of where mods are stored. If mods are missing, BMM can download them automatically from the ServerRepo (if available). If a file was merely moved by mistake, BMM will find and restore it locally without downloading anything.
faq.aOneClick: Only direct download links (DDL) are compatible. A DDL starts the download immediately without going through an intermediate page. GitHub 'Releases' links or direct links to a file on a private server are perfect.
faq.aPat_intro: A Personal Access Token (PAT) lets you download more than 60 mods/hour from GitHub. Here's how to create one:
faq.aPat_s1: Log in to github.com with your account.
faq.aPat_s3: Scroll down in the left menu to Developer settings (very bottom).
faq.aPat_s6: Give it a name (e.g. BMM Downloads), choose an expiry, and check only public_repo under repo.
faq.aPat_s7: Click Generate token, copy it (it starts with ghp_) and paste it into the GitHub PAT field in BMM Settings.
faq.aPat_warn: Never share your token! It grants access to your GitHub account.
faq.aRepo: The Server Repo is a feature that allows you to host your own mod repository or connect to someone else's. It synchronizes mods between users via HTTP, ensuring everyone has the same version and configuration.
faq.aRepoHosting: Yes! BMM supports both approaches. You can host directly from your PC for local sharing (LAN) or use a VPS/dedicated server for 24/7 availability. The application generates all assets required for hosting on any standard web server.
faq.aRepoPublic: You need to forward port 8000 (TCP) on your router, or use the UPnP feature available in the Server Repo tab.
faq.aResumable: BMM splits large files into 4MB chunks. If an error occurs (internet disconnection, crash, or closure), BMM checks which chunks are already validated and only downloads the missing parts.
faq.aSemantic: Classic mode uses standard string matching. Semantic mode is much more advanced: it normalizes your query (removes accents/case), splits it into keywords, and performs a weighted intersection. This allows it to index not only titles but also the full Tasky descriptions and hidden metadata inside interactive diagrams, showing a match percentage for partial results.
faq.aServerSeed: The Server Seed is a secret string that sets your server's identity. Ban lists and whitelist rules are tied to it, so they survive restarts and redeploys. Leave it empty when exporting to generate one, or paste a previous seed to reuse an identity.
faq.aThreads: No. BMM uses a high-performance multi-threaded engine in Rust. Heavy tasks like file copying or hash calculation run in dedicated background threads, keeping the main UI thread (and your PC) fast and responsive.
faq.aTokio: Tokio is Rust's asynchronous runtime. BMM uses it to handle thousands of concurrent I/O operations efficiently, ensuring that file transfers, network requests, and background tasks never block the UI.
faq.aZipTime: BMM performs two intensive tasks: first, it calculates a unique digital fingerprint (BLAKE3) for every file to guarantee perfect synchronization. Second, it compresses everything into a single archive. For 20GB+, this is a massive I/O and CPU operation.
faq.mu.q1: How does BMM know a mod has an update?
faq.mu.a1: Each mod is linked to the repo it came from via a stable repo_mod_id. When you check for updates, BMM compares your installed version to the repo's current version and flags any that differ.
faq.mu.q3: Can I update only some of the mods that have an update?
faq.mu.a3: Yes. The updates modal groups available updates by repo and gives each mod a checkbox. Tick exactly the ones you want; the "Update N mod(s)" button updates only your selection via delta-sync (only changed files download).
faq.mu.q4: What is repo_mod_id and where do I find it?
faq.mu.a4: It's the mod's stable id inside a repo, the same across versions, so BMM can match "your mod" to "the newer mod in the repo". Repo hosts copy it from Server Repo → "Update an existing repo". Mod authors set it with an "id" field in bmm.json.
faq.mu.q5: Can BMM check for mod updates automatically?
faq.mu.a5: Yes. Set a "Mod update check interval" (minutes) in Settings, or 0 for manual only. Mods with an update get an "Update" tag.
faq.mu.q6: A repo couldn't be reached during the check. Is that a problem?
faq.mu.a6: No. BMM lists unreachable repos as errors in the updates modal so you know which to retry. Other repos are still checked.

faq.qDocker: What is Docker and why does BMM use it?
faq.aDocker: Docker packs the BMM server and its dependencies into an isolated container: one command starts it on any OS (Windows, Linux, macOS), with nothing to install by hand.
faq.aNgrok: ngrok creates an encrypted tunnel between your local machine and the Internet. Without opening ports on your router, clients access your server via a public HTTPS URL (e.g. https://abc123.ngrok-free.app). Ideal for home hosting.
faq.aNgrok.warn: On the free plan, the URL changes every time ngrok restarts. Use a paid plan or custom domain for a stable URL.
faq.qVps: VPS vs home PC: what are the differences?
faq.aVps: A VPS gives you a fixed public IP, 24/7 uptime and dedicated bandwidth for ~3–10€/month. A home PC is free but has a dynamic IP (needs ngrok or UPnP) and depends on your machine being on.
faq.qDockerUpdate: How do I update the Docker server?
faq.aDockerUpdate: Updating the BMM server with Docker takes 3 commands. Your data (mods, bans, config) is stored in the ./data volume and is not affected.

Copy the folder to your host (Windows or Linux/Docker) and run the start script: it installs dependencies (npm install) then starts the server (npm start). Node.js is required on the host.

docs.docker.subtitle: Containerisation with ngrok or Cloudflare tunnel to expose your server
docs.docker.whatDesc: Docker is a containerization platform that packages the BMM server and all its dependencies into an isolated box called a container. The server behaves identically on any system — Windows, Linux, macOS — without any manual installation.
docs.docker.tunnelDesc: If you host at home (no fixed IP or no router access), ngrok creates an encrypted tunnel between your local machine and the Internet. Your clients connect to a public URL (e.g. https://abc123.ngrok-free.app) and traffic is forwarded to your server.
docs.docker.tunnelWarn: On the free plan, the ngrok URL changes on every restart. Use a paid plan or a custom domain for a permanent URL.
docs.docker.cfDesc: Free alternative to ngrok — a persistent Cloudflare tunnel with a stable URL on the free plan. No port forwarding needed.

faq.docker.dataNote: Your data in ./data is never deleted during an update.
faq.qCloudflare: Cloudflare Tunnel vs ngrok: what is the difference?
faq.aCloudflare: Both tools create an encrypted tunnel from your machine to the Internet without opening router ports. ngrok is simpler to set up but the URL changes on every restart on the free plan. Cloudflare Tunnel (cloudflared) gives you a stable subdomain for free (requires a Cloudflare account and a domain). For a permanent home-hosting URL, Cloudflare Tunnel is the better long-term option.
faq.aCloudflare.warn: Cloudflare Tunnel requires a domain name registered in Cloudflare DNS. If you don't have a domain, ngrok quick-start is faster.

docs.modStructure.paths3intro: Every profile in BMM relies on 3 paths you configure once:
docs.modStructure.pathGameDesc: Where the game is installed. BMM copies active mod files here.
docs.modStructure.pathModsDesc: The folder where you store all your mods. BMM scans it to build your list.
docs.modStructure.pathBackupDesc: BMM saves the original game files here before replacing them.
docs.modStructure.activateTitle: What happens when you activate a mod
docs.modStructure.activateSteps:
• BMM scans the mod folder and lists all its files.
  • For each file, if a game original exists at the same path and hasn't been backed up yet, BMM copies it to the backup folder.
  • BMM then copies the mod file into the game folder, at the exact matching path.
  • The mod is active — the game sees the mod files in their normal location.
docs.modStructure.deactivateTitle: What happens when you deactivate a mod
docs.modStructure.deactivateSteps:
• BMM removes the files it copied into the game folder.
  • If a backup existed, it is restored — the game gets its original files back.
  • If multiple mods were active on the same file (stacking), BMM restores the previous mod's file.
docs.modStructure.ruleDesc: Each mod file must have the same relative sub-path as its target in the game. BMM uses this to know exactly where to copy. The mod only needs to contain the files it changes.

docs.symlinks.title: How symbolic links work
docs.symlinks.desc: When you enable a mod in BMM, here is what actually happens:
docs.symlinks.step1: BMM scans the mod folder and reconstructs the folder tree
docs.symlinks.step2: For each file/folder, BMM creates a symbolic link in the game folder pointing to your mod
docs.symlinks.step3: The game sees the files as if they were really in its folder — without copying
docs.symlinks.step4: Disabling the mod just removes the symbolic links — your original files are intact
docs.symlinks.warn: Symbolic links require administrator rights on Windows (or developer mode enabled). BMM will ask to elevate permissions if needed. Never manually delete files in the game folder if they are BMM links — always use the "Disable" button in BMM.

tut.basics.integrity.s3.title: When a check fails
tut.basics.integrity.s3.text:
A failed check usually means a game update overwrote a mod file, or a bad download. To fix it:
  • Re-activate the mod (Off then On) to re-copy its files.
  • If the source is damaged too, re-add the mod from a fresh archive.
:warn:

Integrity only checks files BMM installed. For game files, use the launcher's "verify files".

docs.diagram.scheduler.title: Scheduling & Automation
docs.diagram.scheduler.node.TRIGGER.desc: Choose when the task fires: every N minutes/hours, daily/weekly/monthly at a time, once at a date, on BMM start, or manual only.
docs.diagram.scheduler.node.OSTASK.desc: Optional: BMM registers a Windows Scheduled Task that re-launches it via a bmm://schedule/run link so the task fires even when the app was closed.
docs.diagram.scheduler.node.ENGINE.desc: While BMM is open a timer checks each enabled task and runs the ones that are due. Tasks persist to schedules.json.
docs.diagram.scheduler.node.STEPS.desc: A workflow is an ordered list of building blocks executed top to bottom. Blocks can nest (inside if/else branches).
docs.diagram.scheduler.node.ACTION.desc: Activate a profile/modpack, enable/disable a mod, scan, set a theme, launch an app, show a notification, run a custom command, or fire a bmm:// deeplink.
docs.diagram.scheduler.node.COND.desc: Branch on app state: profile active, mod enabled, modpack active, app running, file exists, day/time, command succeeds — with an optional NOT.
docs.diagram.scheduler.node.WAIT.desc: Pause the workflow until a state is reached (e.g. all mods active, an app is running) with a timeout, then continue — perfect for 'enable modpack, wait until ready, then launch'.
docs.diagram.scheduler.node.DONE.desc: When the workflow finishes BMM records the run time/result and shows a toast. Share automations with others via a .BMMPA file.
docs.diagram.updateSystem.title: Update System
docs.diagram.updateSystem.node.REPO.desc: Mods synced from a Server Repo carry a stable repo_mod_id; the repo manifest is the source of truth for new versions.
docs.diagram.updateSystem.node.DIRECT.de: A mod can instead point to one or more direct download URLs; BMM watches them for content changes (size/hash) as a fallback source.
docs.diagram.updateSystem.node.CHECK.des: Triggered manually or on an interval; each unique source is queried once and unreachable sources are reported, not silently ignored.
docs.diagram.updateSystem.node.FETCH.des: BMM reads the repo manifest, or for direct links inspects the file (HEAD / size / hash) to learn its current state.
docs.diagram.updateSystem.node.COMPARE.d: Installed state is compared against the source: repo version, or the file's sha256 / BLAKE3 content signature for direct links.
docs.diagram.updateSystem.node.DETECT.de: If they differ, BMM tags the mod and shows 'BMM may have detected an update' with the change details — it never overwrites silently.
docs.diagram.updateSystem.node.REDL.desc: You pick what to update; repo mods delta-sync only changed files, direct links re-download the file. Then it re-checks.
BMM's own updater reads an update-manifest.json from the GitHub release (HTTPS), listing each file and its sha256.
docs.diagram.updateSystem.node.VERIFY.de: Every file URL must be HTTPS and is verified against its sha256 before being applied; path traversal is rejected (CWE-494/22).
docs.diagram.updateSystem.node.APPLY.des: Verified files are written to a temp location then moved into place; unchanged files are skipped.
tut.other.updates.title: Update sources
tut.other.updates.s1.title: Keeping mods current
tut.other.updates.s1.text: Mods synced from a Server Repo remember their source, so BMM can tell you when a newer version is out.
tut.other.updates.s2.title: Give it a download link
tut.other.updates.s2.text: No repo? Add direct download links on a mod. BMM watches them and shows 'BMM may have detected an update'. It never overwrites silently.
tut.other.updates.s3.title: Check, then apply
tut.other.updates.s3.text: Use Check for updates (manual or on an interval). Pick exactly which mods to update; repo mods delta-sync only the changed files. See the 'Update System' diagram in Help for the full picture.
tut.other.automation.title: Scheduling and automation
tut.other.automation.s1.title: Let BMM do it without you
tut.other.automation.s1.text: In Settings → Planification & automatisation you can schedule BMM actions, once or recurring. E.g. 'every morning at 8h, activate my DCS profile'.
tut.other.automation.s2.title: Build a workflow
tut.other.automation.s2.text: Click Load example to build a ready-made automation: a LOOP that shows a notification 3 times, every hour. Inspect the trigger (WHEN) and the action (WHAT), then Save. It starts disabled: flip the toggle on the card.
tut.other.automation.s3.title: Wait for the app to be ready
tut.other.automation.s3.text: The real power: 'enable a modpack, WAIT UNTIL all its mods are active, THEN launch the game'. Conditions can check profiles, mods, a running app, a file, the time, and more.
tut.other.automation.s4.title: Run it anytime, or share it
tut.other.automation.s4.text: Tick 'Run even when BMM is closed' to register a Windows task. Export your automations as a .BMMPA file to share them. Full details are in the 'Scheduling & Automation' diagram in Help.

faq.cust.q1: How do I customize the navigation bar?
faq.cust.a1: Open Settings → the toolbar at the top of the cards → "Customize navigation". You can drag to reorder tabs, hide or rename them, group them into sections, and add your own buttons (open an internal tab, a dialog, an external URL, or a custom page). Pick any icon, and share your layout via a bmm:// link.
faq.cust.a2: Custom pages are tiny HTML/CSS/JS/WASM apps you add to the navbar. Create one from the "Custom pages" section of the Customize navigation editor. Each page renders inside BMM, in the content area, while the navbar stays available.
faq.cust.q3: Are custom pages safe? Can they access my mods or files?
faq.cust.a3: No. Every page runs in a strict sandbox (isolated iframe, opaque origin, locked-down Content-Security-Policy). It cannot reach BMM, your mods, your files, the system, the network or other pages. Its only link is the bmm API, and every capability is denied until you grant it for that page.
faq.cust.q4: Can a custom page access the internet or store data?
faq.cust.a4: Only if you allow it. In the Custom pages list, each page has toggles: storage (a private 2 MB key/value store, namespaced to that page), notify (BMM toasts), internet (GET only, and only to the exact origins you allow-list), and app info (a few non-sensitive read-only values). Everything is off until you turn it on. Full API docs are in the "Custom Pages API" tab.
faq.cust.q5: An external URL button shows a blank page. Why?
faq.cust.a5: Some sites (YouTube, Google…) forbid being embedded in a frame (their server sends X-Frame-Options / frame-ancestors). That is the sites choice and cannot be bypassed. Use the "Open in browser" button in the pages top bar, or pick a site that allows embedding.

docs.pagesApi.intro: Custom pages are small HTML/CSS/JS/WASM apps you add to the navbar (Settings → Customize navigation → Custom pages). Each page runs in a fully isolated sandbox. A page cannot reach BMM, your mods, files, the system, the network, or any other page. Its only link to BMM is the global bmm object, and every method requires a permission you grant per-page (everything is denied by default).
docs.pagesApi.capStorage: bmm.storage.* — a private key/value store (2 MB), namespaced to this page only.
docs.pagesApi.capNet: bmm.fetch() — GET, but only to the origins you explicitly allow-list for the page. Once granted, a plain fetch() to those origins works too.
docs.pagesApi.capRead: bmm.read() — a few non-sensitive values (app name/version/platform/lang, current theme). Never your data, files, or settings.
docs.pagesApi.writeP: Inline event handlers (onclick="…") and inline <script> are blocked by the page CSP. Put your code in the JS box and use addEventListener. The bmm object is available globally. WASM works: WebAssembly.instantiateStreaming(fetch(module.wasm)) can load a .wasm that ships inside the page (own-bundle fetch is allowed; the internet is not, unless granted).
docs.pagesApi.secNote: Security: a denied call rejects with permission_denied; an internet call to a non-allow-listed origin rejects with origin_not_allowed. There is no way for a page to read BMM internals, run system code, or touch another page's data.
docs.pagesApi.start1: Open Settings → Customize navigation → Custom pages and click Create page.
docs.pagesApi.start2: Fill the HTML, CSS and JS boxes. Your JS goes into app.js; inline onclick/<script> are blocked, so wire events with addEventListener.
docs.pagesApi.start3: Grant the permissions the page needs (use a preset: Strict / Mid / Low), and for internet add the allowed origins.
docs.pagesApi.start4: Add a navbar button of type Custom page pointing at it. Re-open the page (switch tab and back) after changing permissions so the new rules apply.
docs.pagesApi.start5: Need a binary asset (e.g. a .wasm)? Use Import file on the page, then load it with a relative URL (fetch('module.wasm')).

docs.pagesApi.cRead: A safe read-only value (see scopes below), or null.
docs.pagesApi.callsNote: Every call returns a Promise. If the permission isn’t granted it rejects with permission_denied (and a toast names the missing permission).
docs.pagesApi.cClipWrite: Copies text to the system clipboard. Resolves true.
docs.pagesApi.cSystem: Safe read-only system facts (see shape below). No filesystem, processes, or shell.
docs.pagesApi.capClipboard: bmm.clipboard.* — read/write the system clipboard (on a user action).
docs.pagesApi.capSystem: bmm.system.info() — safe, read-only hardware/OS facts (OS, arch, CPU count, RAM, uptime). Never the filesystem, processes, shell, or your identity.

tut.quick.meta.title: The five-minute tour
tut.quick.meta.desc: What BMM is, one stop per big idea. No actions, no modals - just where everything lives. The longer tutorials teach you to USE each piece; this one makes sure you know it exists.
tut.quick.tour.title: The tour
tut.quick.tour.s1.title: The Library is home
tut.quick.tour.s1.text: Every mod BMM knows about lives here - with its version, author, tags and state. A green toggle means the mod's files are applied to the game right now; grey means they are safely stored, ready to apply. Nothing you do in this list touches the game until you flip a toggle.
tut.quick.tour.s2.title: Mods come in here
tut.quick.tour.s2.text: Add a mod imports from a folder or an archive. BMM copies the files into its own storage and fingerprints every one of them - which is what later lets it verify nothing got corrupted, detect conflicts, and undo cleanly.
tut.quick.tour.s3.title: Verify is your safety net
tut.quick.tour.s3.text: This re-hashes every stored file and compares it against the fingerprint taken at import. A mod that passes is byte-for-byte what you imported; one that fails has been changed, corrupted, or half-deleted - and BMM tells you which files.
tut.quick.tour.s4.title: Profiles keep games apart
tut.quick.tour.s4.text: A profile is one game (or one playthrough): its own mod list, its own game folder, its own backups. Switching profiles switches everything at once, so two games - or two setups of the same game - can never contaminate each other.
tut.quick.tour.s5.title: Modpacks are recipes
tut.quick.tour.s5.text: A modpack is a named set of mods you apply in one click - 'my multiplayer set', 'vanilla plus'. It records which mods and in what order, so a working combination is something you can come back to, share, or ship in a repo.
tut.quick.tour.s6.title: The Mapper untangles folders
tut.quick.tour.s6.text: Some mods ship with the wrong folder layout for your game. The Mapper shows the mod's structure next to the game's, and lets you re-map where each part lands - without editing the mod itself. The original files stay untouched.
tut.quick.connect.title: Connecting & beyond
tut.quick.connect.s1.title: Server repos: mods from a URL
tut.quick.connect.s1.text: Paste a repository URL here and BMM can pull a whole curated mod set - with integrity hashes, so every download is verified. If the server has no repo.json at all, BMM reads its folder index instead and installs the mods marked as unverified, telling you exactly what that means.
tut.quick.connect.s2.title: Fetch first, decide after
tut.quick.connect.s2.text: Fetch downloads nothing but the manifest: you see the repo's name, author, signature status and every profile it offers before a single mod file moves. Protected repo? There is a password row right under the URL field.
tut.quick.connect.s3.title: Settings - and the look
tut.quick.connect.s3.text: Language, backups, Tasky the mascot, performance, themes - all here. Tip: press Ctrl+K anywhere and type what you want ('style', 'export', 'verify'...) - the command palette reaches almost everything faster than any menu.
tut.quick.connect.s4.title: When in doubt: Help & Other
tut.quick.connect.s4.text: The full documentation lives in the app - how syncing verifies files, what the Mapper actually does, 41 interactive diagrams. That's the tour! The other tutorials in the hub go deeper on each stop, whenever you want them.

docs.diagram.customPages.title: Custom pages (the sandbox)
docs.diagram.customPages.node.NAV.desc: A page you added appears in the navbar like any other view. Nothing about it is special until it is opened.
docs.diagram.customPages.node.FRAME.desc: The page renders inside a sandboxed iframe, not in BMM itself. It shares no window, no globals and no DOM with the app around it.
docs.diagram.customPages.node.INDEX.desc: The entry document. BMM writes it from the HTML you type, wrapped in a head that links the shared stylesheet and the SDK — so what you author is a body, not a whole document.
docs.diagram.customPages.node.SUBS.desc: A page can hold several documents. Link between them with an ordinary relative link (<a href="about.html">); each one is generated by the same head builder as the index, so it shares the CSS, the script, the permissions and the storage.
docs.diagram.customPages.node.ASSETS.des: Images, fonts, JSON, even a .wasm module can be imported into the bundle and loaded with a relative path. The name and extension are validated and the size is capped.
docs.diagram.customPages.node.SDK.desc: The only channel out. Your code calls bmm.* rather than touching the app: there is no other object to reach for, and inline handlers are blocked by the policy below, so scripts live in app.js.
docs.diagram.customPages.node.PROTO.desc: A dedicated protocol serves the bundle. It refuses any path containing "..", then resolves symlinks and checks the result still sits inside the page folder — so a page can only ever read its own files.
docs.diagram.customPages.node.CSP.desc: Every response carries a Content-Security-Policy built for that page. Scripts may load only from the bundle itself, which is why inline onclick does not run and why a page cannot pull code from the internet.
docs.diagram.customPages.node.STORE.desc: Granted pages get a private key/value store, keyed by page id. One page cannot read another’s.
docs.diagram.customPages.node.NET.desc: A page with the network grant reaches the origins you allow-listed for it, and nothing else — the policy is relaxed for those hosts only, and only while the grant is held.
docs.diagram.customPages.node.DENY.desc: No mods, no profiles, no files on disk, no arbitrary network. A page starts with nothing and is given exactly what you grant it, one capability at a time.
docs.diagram.deeplinks.title: Deep links (bmm://)
docs.diagram.deeplinks.node.LINK.desc: Anywhere a link can live — a web page, a scheduled task, another app, a QR code. 46 routes exist; the reference lists every one.
docs.diagram.deeplinks.node.OS.desc: The system hands the URL to BMM. Only one instance runs, so a link opened while BMM is already up goes to the running window rather than starting a second copy.
docs.diagram.deeplinks.node.ROUTER.desc: One handler reads the action and its query string and dispatches. An unknown action is refused with a message rather than ignored.
docs.diagram.deeplinks.node.DIRECT.desc: Links whose meaning is unambiguous do the thing: activate a profile, enable a mod, apply a theme, run a scheduled task, restart. They report what happened.
docs.diagram.deeplinks.node.UI.desc: Anything with consequences opens the matching screen with the fields already filled in, and waits for you to confirm. Generating or publishing a repo works this way on purpose — so an upload is visible and cancellable rather than happening in the background.
docs.diagram.deeplinks.node.APIL.desc: One route is a bridge onto the local HTTP API: it takes a path under /api/ and forwards the call. The path is validated first — anything not starting with /api/ is refused.
docs.diagram.deeplinks.node.TOKEN.desc: The bridge does not bypass anything: the call goes through the same token and permission checks a direct HTTP request would face.
docs.diagram.deeplinks.node.TOAST.desc: Every route ends in a visible result — a toast, a screen, or an error naming what was wrong. A link that quietly did nothing is the failure this avoids.
